received_concept_map.received_body:
A **Document** is a structured knowledge artefact recognised by the Documentation Framework.

A document may evolve over time while preserving its identity.

Document identity is therefore independent of document revisions or editions.

---

A **Document Identity** is the permanent architectural identity assigned to a document.

It uniquely distinguishes one document from every other document managed within the Documentation Framework.

Document Identity remains constant throughout the complete lifetime of the document.

---

An **Identity** is the persistent architectural characteristic that allows an entity to be uniquely recognised independently of its mutable properties.

Within this component, identity refers exclusively to the identity of documents.

---

An **Identifier** is the canonical representation of a document identity.

It provides the human-readable and machine-readable form through which the identity is referenced.

The internal representation of an identifier is defined by the Document Identity Specification.

---

An **Identity Domain** defines the architectural scope within which document identities are guaranteed to be unique.

The Documentation Framework defines the framework itself as the canonical identity domain.

Implementations may introduce additional domains provided that architectural uniqueness is preserved.

---

The **Identity Lifetime** represents the period during which a document identity exists.

The lifetime begins when the identity is assigned and ends only when the document permanently ceases to exist within the architectural context.

Changes to the document never imply changes to its identity.

---

**Identity Stability** is the property that guarantees that the identity of a document never changes after assignment.

Stability ensures that references remain valid independently of document evolution.

---

**Identity Uniqueness** guarantees that no two documents possess the same identity within the same identity domain.

Uniqueness is an architectural requirement.

---

**Identity Permanence** guarantees that once assigned, an identity shall never be reassigned to another document.

Identity survives every normal modification of the document.

---

An **Identity Reference** is the use of a document identity by another component to establish an architectural relationship.

References never redefine identity.

They only reuse identities defined by this component.

---

findings.before: Family=Documentation is the structural area while Component=Document Identity records component membership. Type=Architecture is already valid for conceptual foundations. Received V1.0 R0,Canonical/Baseline1.0,English and Author Arnaldo Figueira are declarations without supplied approval or selection events.
findings.proposal: Use Family=Document Identity,matching Component and retained Type=Architecture;preserve DF-DID-002,path,original author/received declarations and absent original date. Attribute actual successor contribution separately from user authorization/review/approval. Assess actual contracts for Version,increment Revision monotonically and use Draft/Baseline Not assigned;no Class or new allocation invented.
findings.closure_criterion: Header/rationale follows canonical component membership/four Types,stable identity and actual attribution/history without inherited Canonical approval or Baseline selection.

findings.before: §2 requires each document permanent identity and §9 guarantees every document complete-lifecycle identification without normalized/functional scope. General Identity/document/component usages do not distinguish physical files,exact editions,Template/Metadata entities or graph-edge identities.
findings.proposal: Apply all-location README.md/CHANGELOG.md/ArchitecturalMilestones.md normalization exclusion while retaining content/reference/history/hash checks. Define normalized logical document identity separately from files,editions,descriptors and other entity-domain keys;qualify Identity as the general concept and Document Identity as its documentary use. Document endpoints/nodes use document identity,other entities/edges use their own appropriate contracts. No normalized ID/Metadata Element allocation is inferred for excluded files or every entity.
findings.closure_criterion: Document/Identity/scope and consumer clauses consistently respect normalized applicability and distinct entity kinds without treating all represented knowledge assets as normalized documents or graph edges as document identities.

findings.before: §3.5 correctly identifies domain uniqueness but grants implementations additional domains with only generic architectural uniqueness. §3.2 describes uniqueness across managed documents and §3.4 delegates internal representation solely to Specification without distinguishing logical identity/key/string or current corpus allocation convention and pending schema differences.
findings.proposal: Define Domain+Identifier qualification,canonical identifier representation and actual domain/allocation ownership. In the DF corpus,registered stable DF-SSS-NNN series are independent of current Family/Type/path/edition;qualified domain uniqueness is not bare-string global uniqueness or silent external-domain registration. Other-domain use requires explicit qualified owner rules. Refer to DID Architecture/Schema/Constraints/Specification for actual representation contracts without duplicating a complete schema,algorithm or guessed mandatory field. Preserve pending schema integration and no actual allocation/migration in this source.
findings.closure_criterion: Concepts consistently distinguish logical identity/domain/canonical representation,scope uniqueness and corpus namespace meaning,retain real owner contracts and do not grant arbitrary domains or invent a merged schema/catalog.

findings.before: §3.6 ends identity existence when the document ceases to exist;§3.7 says stability ensures reference validity independent of evolution. Active lifetime,retirement/history/reservations and live resolver/content availability are not separated. Absolute unchanged identity wording does not address authorized necessary representation/allocation contract migration.
findings.proposal: Separate active document/identity-record use from retained historical identity associations/reservations and non-reuse. Preserve valid assigned identity during ordinary evolution;retirement does not permit another document to reuse it and preserved references do not guarantee deployed resolution or retrieved content. Necessary authorized migration first reconciles governing rules with identity/domain owners and records old-new/same-document/alias/reservation/collision/history/edition/consumer/transition evidence;immutable snapshots remain pinned and no arbitrary reassignment or actual migration occurs here.
findings.closure_criterion: Lifetime/Stability/Permanence and governance/summary clauses consistently preserve retirement/history/non-reuse,qualify actual reference evidence and necessary controlled migration without finite-lifetime erasure,snapshot retargeting or universal retrieval guarantees.

findings.before: The §4 chain mixes possession,representation and component reference without domain/reference subjects or explicit relationship-kind limits. Registry dependency is unscoped;Relationships owns associations while Graph represents identities as nodes and edges. Required consumption versus association/projection/execution and exact-edition target evidence are unspecified.
findings.proposal: Type the original view as selected conceptual relationships with explicit subjects/owner meanings,not a serial required/runtime graph. Distinguish document-reference association from immutable key and exact-edition targeting;Relationships owns typed records and other endpoints use their own domains. Required consumer→provider uses state scope/source/interface and follow support/same-Layer/prohibited-cycle rules;preserve apparent DID↔Metadata claims already recorded in Architecture as unresolved rather than asserting universal independence. Registry/Graph projections retain provenance/freshness,document identity applies to document nodes,not edges;identity alone selects no Baseline member.
findings.closure_criterion: All view/reference/consumer meanings are accurate and explicit;actual indispensable contracts/cycles remain visible,exact-edition and endpoint domains qualified,and no universal routing,serial graph or global acyclicity is certified.

findings.before: §5 contrasts identity as permanent/immutable/unique with Metadata mutable/repeated/Version dependent without distinguishing immutable key,represented descriptor values and owner meanings. §8 says the whole component defines concepts only while delegating syntax/validation/governance to subsequent documents within that same component. Governance is described as managing operations without executor boundaries.
findings.proposal: State this document's conceptual scope rather than restricting the whole component. Identity owns identity/domain/allocation meanings;Metadata defines/represents descriptors under semantic owners,with Dictionary defining,Schema organizing,Profile constraining and Instance values under one effective Profile. A represented identity value remains subject to identity constraints;metadata properties can have their own identity/lifecycle/uniqueness and are not universally Version dependent. Definitions/contracts are separate from DMS/tool/manual operations and CMS change scope;document/identity-record states and exact edition facts remain distinct. Keep actual Metadata Model/Dictionary discrepancies pending rather than populating fields or merging schemas.
findings.closure_criterion: Document/component and identity/descriptor/entity lifecycle boundaries are consistent throughout purpose,table,scope and consumers;no competing authority,universal metadata mutability/version rule,automatic executor or catalog/Profile creation is introduced.

findings.before: Identity Independence forbids dependence on all implementation concerns and requires identities globally understandable. Conceptual technology neutrality,logical representation/adapter constraints and actual human/machine interpretation/resolution are not separated. The source's boundary wording can prohibit legitimate logical contract detail.
findings.proposal: Preserve technology-neutral conceptual meaning while permitting applicable logical domain/canonicalization/reference/representation and integration constraints in responsible sources. Concept scope can explain those boundaries without supplying generation/storage algorithms. Actual adapters/executors and examined scope determine conformance;format/repository independence does not guarantee universal interoperability or future availability. Preserve compatibility where feasible and assess necessary contract changes with owners/consumers/dependencies/transitions and monotonic Revision.
findings.closure_criterion: Independence/Identifier/principle/summary wording separates conceptual obligations from concrete representation/executor evidence and controlled evolution,without universal portability,harmless extension or automatic outcomes.

findings.before: Concepts are said to ensure/guarantee uniqueness,reference validity and every-document lifecycle consistency. Applicable requirements,examined bytes/source scopes and actual outcomes/approval are not distinguished;received Canonical status and conceptual definition can be misread as completed peer/implementation conformance.
findings.proposal: Retain explicit conceptual/domain requirements and responsibility while bounding conclusions by actual rules,exact artifacts/editions/context,checks,observations,executor,coverage and unmet/pending conditions. Source Type/title/presence/status or local PASS confers no implemented allocation/resolution,approval,publication or Baseline. Preserve current peer schema/state/cardinality/assignment/reciprocal requirements and global records. Actual contribution,authorization,review,validation and approval differ;later bytes require independent assessment with no inherited results or responsibility for consequences of a changed product.
findings.closure_criterion: Requirements/qualities and achieved evidence are consistently distinguished;local correction closes only its declared findings/exact source,not full peer/global conformance or product/future-result guarantees.

findings.before: Eight §7 identity-property labels are stated as always applicable and are not mapped to actual framework principles/domain constraints. Unique/permanent/immutable properties require domain and subject qualification;globally understandable is a bounded interoperability objective rather than a new formal AP.
findings.proposal: Preserve all eight received property labels with applicable role/owner mappings:identity/domain preservation and non-reuse contracts plus AP-010 Stable Identity;technology/repository/implementation neutrality as AP-003 applications;global understandability as qualified representation/evidence objective. Do not fabricate property IDs/APs or imply full24-principle conformance. Preserve all eleven core-concept titles/anchors with explicit applicability/evidence boundaries.
findings.closure_criterion: Every property and core concept is accounted for with real owner/application scope,without universal always-guarantees,new AP IDs,changed original anchors or automatic conformance.
